description:
Bound `apply_bulk_update` session opens to the matched issues that actually need a change, matching the guarantee already tested for automatic transitions, and extend the benchmark harness with a bulk-mutation scenario measuring the fixed behavior.

## Background

`apply_bulk_update` (`crates/jit/src/commands/bulk_update.rs`, roughly lines 161-197) currently opens a preflight session and a publication session for every filter-matched issue before knowing whether anything changes — cost 2·|matched|. `check_auto_transitions` already demonstrates the correct shape: a cheap in-memory eligibility prefilter that can only skip, never authorize, plus an authoritative recheck inside the session.

The fix adds a pure `UpdateOperations::is_provable_noop(&Issue) -> bool` prefilter over the already-listed issues. It is deliberately Issue-local and no-op-only: it skips an issue exactly when every operation's target value already holds (state equal, labels present/absent, priority, gate and assignee state), all decidable from the listed `Issue` alone. Potentially invalid updates are not prefiltered — they still open sessions so the same authoritative in-session validation produces the same per-issue error results as today. Repository-dependent validity never moves out of the session, and the prefilter only skips, never authorizes (the same TOCTOU-safe property as the auto-transitions guard).

The session-open bound: sessions opened = C·|{matched issues that are not provable no-ops}|, where C is the per-mutation session constant (currently 2: preflight plus publication). The budget test derives C from a single-issue baseline run rather than hardcoding it, so later combinator refactors cannot invalidate it. The test reuses the same session-open counting probe the auto-transitions budget test uses (`test_check_auto_transitions_opens_sessions_only_for_eligible_backlog_issues` in `crates/jit/src/commands/issue.rs`), which counts the once-per-session-open failure point. It seeds K matched issues of which K-J already hold their target values and asserts C·J session opens, not C·K.

After the fix lands, the benchmark harness `scripts/benchmark-session-cost.sh` gains a bulk-mutation scenario (a filtered `issue update`) recorded in the artifact's `commands` array, so the artifact captures the fixed behavior.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `apply_bulk_update` opens sessions only for matched issues that are not provable no-ops; for K matched issues of which J require a change, session opens equal C·J where C is the per-mutation session constant.
- [hard] REQ-02: `UpdateOperations::is_provable_noop` is a pure, Issue-local predicate that skips an issue exactly when every operation's target value already holds; it never authorizes an update and never moves repository-dependent validity out of the session.
- [hard] REQ-03: An issue whose update is potentially invalid still opens a session and yields the same per-issue error result as before the change.
- [hard] REQ-04: The session-budget test derives C from a single-issue baseline run rather than hardcoding it, counts session opens via the existing once-per-session-open failure-point probe, and asserts C·J for K seeded issues with K-J already at their target values.
- [hard] REQ-05: The benchmark harness records a bulk-mutation scenario in its artifact, measuring the post-fix behavior.

## Notes

The fix is behavior-preserving for update results: only the number of sessions opened for provable no-ops changes. Do not hardcode C; a single-issue baseline run yields it.
title: Bulk-update eligibility prefilter and session-budget test
